sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily upon first access.
sketches.resonance: Declaring someone as an `object` means the language itself guarantees there will never be another — uniqueness enforced by the compiler.

sketches.mechanism: A type declared with no constructors (`Void`) can never be instantiated — values of that type cannot exist at the term level, yet the type itself can be named and passed around.
sketches.resonance: We can speak of what can never exist; the type system permits naming the impossible while forbidding its construction.

sketches.mechanism: The `weak` reference modifier means the runtime may deallocate the referent at any time, and accessing it yields an Optional — presence that may already be nil.
sketches.resonance: Holding someone weakly means every time you reach for them, you must confront the possibility they are already gone.
